product.purpose: The product turns a submitted request into a validated result.
boundaries: It does not own upstream identity.
outcomes: A user receives a validated result.
outputs: A result or an actionable error

decisions.rationale: A real flow connects product purpose to implementation.

components.name: Request entrypoint
components.role: Accepts the product request and starts the use-case path.
components.boundary: It does not own validation rules or result formatting.
components.why: It gives product input one stable entry into the application flow.

components.name: Validator
components.role: Checks whether the request meets the product contract.
produces: Accepted data or an actionable error
components.boundary: It does not own transport concerns or user-interface rendering.
components.why: It keeps the product rule in one place before downstream work begins.

sections.title: Catch-up
sections.body: A user submits a request. The product validates it and returns a result.

sections.title: The Gist
sections.body: Validation turns an untrusted request into a result the product can safely use.

sections.title: How It Fits Together
sections.body: The entrypoint accepts the request. The validator checks it. The result layer returns the outcome.

sections.title: Follow the Data
sections.summary: One request from input to output.

sections.title: In the Code
sections.body: The entrypoint receives the request and passes it to validation before producing the result.

sections.title: Prove It
sections.body: Use the questions below to test the flow.

questions.feedback: Validation is the step that checks the request before the result is produced.

questions.prompt: Which statements describe the product flow?
questions.feedback: The flow begins with a request and includes validation; the unrelated report is not part of this path.
